title: Human Refrigerators Keep People Cool in Japan
paragraphs: Summers in Japan are getting hotter and more humid, and temperatures regularly go above 35°C. To help people cool down quickly, a Japanese company is now selling what some people call a "human refrigerator."
The machine is called the Do Hiemon Box, and it is sold by Trusco Nakayama, a Tokyo company that sells tools and equipment. It went on sale in April 2026.

The Do Hiemon Box is a tall stainless-steel box on wheels, with a window and a bench inside. It is big enough for one person. The inside of the box stays at about 15°C. When a person sits inside, the machine blows very cold air, at about 5°C, onto their head, neck and shoulders. According to the company, people start to feel cooler within five minutes. The machine also turns off by itself after 20 minutes, so that people do not get too cold.

The box is not designed as a place to relax. Instead, it is meant to give quick help to people who are suffering from the heat, especially in places without easy access to air conditioning. It only needs a normal electrical outlet.

Each box costs 1.5 million yen. So far, the company has sold the machines to steel factories, construction sites, golf courses, universities and leisure facilities. After a recent earthquake in Kumamoto, the company also sent some boxes to shelters for people who had to leave their homes.

Fumiaki Matsubara, a manager at Trusco, said that demand for the company's cooling products for workplaces has "roughly doubled every year in recent years." Stricter government rules to prevent heatstroke at work are also increasing demand.
The company has also received questions from Germany and the United States. It thinks shopping malls and summer festivals may also want to use the boxes.
However, the health benefits are based on claims by the company, and they have not been tested by independent scientists.
